items.english: "Oi, boss," came the call, and Nekohachi lifted his eyes from the Koudan Club he had been buried in and turned them toward the voice. He knew by the voice who it was, and that put him at his ease,
notes: "boss" for taishou, Takami's familiar hail. Koudan Club kept as magazine title.

items.english: "Well, Sensei!" putting on a vacant look on purpose. "Fancy meeting you on this tram, eh? So then, some fine nest has turned up round this way, eh?"
notes: su as nest keeps the pun picked up in p4 with Sugamo no su. Sensei kept for Nekohachi's address to Takami. Second eh for sentence-final na.

items.english: "..." That got him straight off, one down. But by now all the passengers around were pricking up their ears, so he called back into himself the feeling from the kouza he had just come off with his hands free. And with all the passengers starting to look like his own customers to him, he felt here he would have to give something back somehow. "That would be it, eh," putting on a suddenly solemn face, and just then with a sidelong glance catching their tram passing in front of the lunatic hospital he made it into material,
notes: kouza kept as stage. Long run-on kept as one pull back into performance because the passengers have become an audience. Tenkyou hospital as lunatic hospital in front of which the tram is passing.

items.english: "In a place like Sugamo there is nothing living but madmen or monsters like Nekohachi, eh."
notes: Keeps third-person Nekohachi and madmen/monster wording stable as load-bearing repetition. eh for na.

items.english: "ha, ha, ha," somebody laughed, and so even in a place like this he got the response he always got. He thought of the place and tried to hold back any further wisecracks on top of it, but somehow his mouth seemed unwilling to agree to it.
notes: Laughter kept thin as ha, ha, ha. Mouth unwilling keeps the compulsion to keep performing even while checking himself.

data.say: Drafted opening tram exchange keeping banter as work and holding nest, kouza, and madmen/monsters wording.
